summary: This document clarifies how policy qualifiers may appear in the certificate policies extension of RPKI resource certificates. RPKI certificates tie Internet number resources, such as IP address blocks, to their holders, and this update removes ambiguity left in RFC 6487.

eli5.summary: Imagine a school ID card with a small note on it. This RFC says exactly what kind of notes are allowed on the special cards that prove who owns which Internet addresses.

questions: what is a policy qualifier in rpki
subtitle: RPKI resource certificates may carry exactly one policy qualifier, a pointer to a Certification Practice Statement.

tldr.problem: RFC 6487 required exactly one policy in RPKI resource certificates but did not say whether policy qualifiers were allowed, while some certificate authorities needed to include them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7318 replaces the text of Section 4.8.9 of RFC 6487 so that exactly one policy qualifier MAY be included, and if present it MUST be the CPS pointer type (id-qt-cps).
tldr.outcome: Certificates with such a qualifier are now within the RPKI profile, and relying parties that do strict validation without this update would wrongly reject them.

today: RFC 7318 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6487. The unit metadata shows nothing obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: The Gap in RFC 6487
sections.content:
RFC 6487 profiles X.509 certificates for the Resource Public Key Infrastructure. It requires the certificate policies extension, defined in RFC 5280, to be present, marked critical, and to include exactly one policy as specified in the RPKI Certificate Policy.

RFC 5280 also lets a policy carry optional PolicyQualifierInfo objects. RFC 6487 neither allows nor disallows them, yet it also says that fields not listed MUST NOT appear in a conforming certificate. Because some RPKI certificate authorities need to include qualifiers, RFC 7318 settles the question.
sections.eli5: The rules did not say whether a small extra note was allowed on the certificate, and some issuers wanted to add one.

sections.title: The Update to Section 4.8.9
sections.content:
The memo gives old and new text for Section 4.8.9 of RFC 6487. The extension MUST still be present, MUST be critical and MUST include exactly one policy. The new text adds that exactly one policy qualifier MAY be included, and if so its policyQualifierId MUST be the Certification Practice Statement pointer type, id-qt-cps.

Following RFC 5280, an optional qualifier is not expected to change the definition of the policy. Accordingly, any qualifier in a resource certificate MUST NOT change the definition of the RPKI Certificate Policy.
sections.eli5: You may add one note, and it must point to the issuer's written practices. It cannot change the rules.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 6487 apply. The qualifier is a URI. Dereferencing it is not required for certificate validation, and doing so could provide a denial-of-service vector, since the target host may be subjected to bogus work. The specification, like RFC 5280, places no processing requirements on the URI.

The update also widens the set of conforming certificates. A relying party doing strict validation per RFC 6487 that does not support this update would incorrectly invalidate RPKI objects that include a policy qualifier.
sections.eli5: Following the link is not needed, and could be used to pester a website. Checkers that do not know about the note might wrongly reject good certificates.
